This kept me entertained for hours. And when I accidentally deleted the game I was playing and had to start all over again, I enjoyed it then also. Now I have the expansion, which lends to a whole different way of playing the game, which adds more interest and a bit of a community feel to it, though I really haven't played much of that bit so far.
I really do enjoy typing, and puzzle games, and have a prior interest in hacking so this really appealed to me on many levels, and didn't let down! 
There are a few odd glitches throughout which mean for some players they can't progress through certain forks of the game. You still get a whole experience, but on a replay and to get the extra achievements, trying to navigate through those glitches is frustrating, and I haven't successfully managed to do so yet. Perhaps in time...?
Overall, though, I really genuinely loved this game and it's become a firm favourite.

[h1][b]IF YOU LIKE THE IDEA OF A GAME FOCUSING ENTIRELY ON A TERMINAL/COMMAND-LINE AND SOME EASY TO MODERATELY DIFFICULT PUZZLES THROWN IN, YOU MAY LIKE THIS GAME.[/b][/h1]
As someone who has a bit of experience with the UNIX terminal and commands, this game had my absolute full attention and felt familiar to me. [b]I've just recently bought this game (yesterday, at the time of writing) and I was absolutely HOOKED and couldn't get away from it. Hacknet is absolutely my style of game! (right now, I've just beaten the base game and will go through the DLC content shortly. but I may fiddle around with the Extensions)[/b]

[h1][b]TARGET[/b][/h1]
Obviously, this game isn't for everyone. A terminal-based game can seem intimidating or uninteresting to someone who has no experience with it before (and even if you do, a terminal-based game may not be that interesting). If the screenshots and description provided by the game do not capture your attention, it's probably not the game for you. But if your curiosity is piqued, it may be a great experience for you.

[h1][b]PUZZLE ELEMENTS AND TUTORIALS[/b][/h1]
Hacknet introduces itself quite well to the uninformed, and doesn't hand-hold. It throws you straight in after a short tutorial on using the terminal and interface, therefore encouraging experimentation with what you have available. By not holding the player's hand, succeeding in the puzzles without any additional help besides what the game provides will give you a sense of accomplishment. However, that can turn some people off, and if it does, it may not be for you.

It is possible to get stuck in several points in the game, but no solution is too far out there and is solvable without a walkthrough. (and I admit, I have, and have consulted a walkthrough but I was extra careful not to look any further ahead than the current task at hand, most of the time I had just forgotten something simple and was able to get back on track quickly).

The puzzles start off pretty easy, leading you on and increasing the difficulty as it goes, pretty much gently guiding you on how to work with the game's unique nature.

At certain times, the tasks can seem repetitive, and to be fair, it is. You are constantly trying to break into a lot of different computers, servers, devices, etc. but that's what it is. It is an accurate representation instead of the flashy Hollywood style hacking seen on film (but it certainly can be flashy when it wants to be and is for certain parts).

[h1][b]STORY[/b][/h1]
The story itself is nothing outstanding, but it certainly fits the theme and style of the game. It's perfect for the game. The story is there for the beginning and the end of your gameplay, giving you purpose to start and an objective to reach near the end. In the middle of the game, you are given freedom to do what you wish. Or PointClicker, if that's your thing (I won't judge!).

[h1][b]MUSIC[/b][/h1]
The music is an absolute fit for Hacknet and I often found myself focusing on the killer beats rather than what's at hand. It also made me quite shaky during the parts that are time-based.

[h1][b]OVERALL[/b][/h1]
Overall, Hacknet is extremely accurate compared to other things that have tried to display this kind of topic before. The elements work wonderfully and the balance between gameplay and the real elements is on point (all the commands given are used at one point or another and no unnecessary garbage is there). To the average person who may not know anything about the terminal, it can be exciting to get into it for the first time not knowing anything and eventually learn (there may be a little higher risk of getting stuck at a point, but that's okay!). To those who are a little familiar with the terminal and commands, you'll feel right at home and understand the game quickly and have a great time with it!

[h1][b]SHOULD YOU GET IT?[/b][/h1]
If this game looks interesting, [b]IT WILL BE FOR YOU.[/b] The terminal looks intimidating from the start, and if that doesn't deter you and the description of the game brings you in further, you [b]WILL[/b] enjoy it!

Okay so, I'm not overly familier with making reviews, however, this is a game I'm going to make one for.

Hacknet is a game about hacking (Bet you couldn't get that from the name eh?)

You play the role of fulfilling the wishes of someone named "Bit". Oh and side onte, Spoilers incoming! 

You learn about the Hacknet OS in the tutorial, learning how to breach systems, and search for more to breach.
You eventually are released from the tutorial (Which you can end early if you know how)
I highly suggest you play the tutorial at minimum of one time, and play it again if you need to brush up on how to play.

Now the tutorial will NOT cover everything you can do, that's okay, you are given tutorial "servers" with that information and you can make little pin notes to help remind you, however, that uses your "system memory" which is used to attack other systems when launching programs designed to do so. 

You have SSH, FTP and many other tools to breach systems which you will gain as you progress in the story.

The DLC is many times more interesting, and if you want to see a real treat and fireworks show, I suggest you go through and have alot of servers from your first playthrough available for what happens at the start of Labrynths. 

Labrynths follows a similar pattern to what the base games does, but with some new twists. You're not longer part of a "large" group, you are not part of a 4 man group (Yourself being the 4th) and you progress through a different storyline and the finale of it, lets just say, I still am curious as to how many other people made the decision for it.

All in all, it's fun, and can be a bit frustrating at times, but that is only on your first couple of play throughs, I strongly recommend playing this because hot damn is this game fun, the music is kickass, and the game is a treat.

Hacknet was a game I devoured. I didn't really put it down from start to stop, except maybe to prepare meals or other daily necessities.
While it indeed is gripping with it's great amount of content and things to do, I feel like I can't complain about it because of its price.
For the price, it's a great experience, even with the DLC, which I would also recommend.

But here we are.
PROS:
-Tutorial is great, even if it is a little handhold-y at times, but after having played it once and starting up a new game, it wasn't that hard to 'bypass' the Tutorial.exe
-While each system the player connects to seem a bit desolated, it makes up for it with a lot of IRC logs written with nice humor and some great junkmail from some nice Nigerian Princes.
-You are only as good as your typing speed and program-time management, nicely skill based.
-There are some missions that require you to make hard decisions but you don't really get anything great out of it, which is a great way to introduce morals in a game, rather than a moral system. "Was it really worth doing that for this?"

CONS:
-While there are a lot of IRC logs and the junkmails are nice, there aren't that many different ones. Only one type of junkmail which is the Nigerian Prince scam.
-Lots of systems, especially the personal ones, feel empty, having only a few folders and files on them compared to what we have on ours, even back in the 00's.
-The visual organizing of the different systems are very annoying and randomised and it's only in the DLC that you actually get a program that makes it neat and organized. But that's a more personal one, I guess.

Honestly, the pros and cons don't really matter, it's a great experience and an easy 20 hours to throw into it. 
I have no idea how big the team, who were working on this, were but I feel they definitely delivered. Some systems are more personal than others and the game's versions of known hacker groups are hilariously immature, except for the Hacking Elites.
There's also a nice cult to hack into, so the amount of research the devs put into this is really impressive.
